stories.title: Mafia Ashraf’s aide killed in broad daylight:Shot at tea shop in Prayagraj; land dispute angle emerges
stories.summary: The incident occurred around 6:30 PM near Bismillah Chowk. Irfan was sitting at a tea shop close to his house when four attackers arrived on two motorcycles. All had covered their faces with gamchas. According to eyewitness accounts, three attackers remained seated on the bikes while one got down, approached Irfan, pulled out a pistol and shot him in the chest at point-blank range. He collapsed on the spot, bleeding heavily. The attackers then brandished the weapon, mounted their bikes and fled. Taken to hospital, declared dead Locals immediately informed Irfan’s family, who live about 250 metres away in Ainuddinpur. His wife and son rushed to the spot and took him to SRN Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The killing led to chaos and fear in the area. See 2 pictures- Family alleges role of gangster-linked accused Irfan was reportedly a close associate of Ashraf Ahmad and had worked as his driver around 12 years ago. His family has accused Asif Durrani (45), his brother Rashid, and others of carrying out the murder. Durrani, a resident of Chakiya, is known to be linked to the gang of Atiq Ahmad. An FIR has been registered at Kareli police station based on a complaint by Irfan’s son, Mohammad Aamir. Land dispute suspected as motive Police said preliminary investigation points to a property dispute as the possible motive. Both Irfan and Durrani were involved in land dealings and had ongoing conflicts over transactions. Officials said the exact reason behind the murder will be confirmed after further investigation. Accused has long criminal history Police records show that Asif Durrani has over 17 cases registered against him at Dhumanganj police station. He has been named in multiple FIRs alongside Atiq Ahmad. In 2020, he was booked in an illegal slaughterhouse case, and in 2021, authorities demolished his house under anti-mafia action. Cases related to witness intimidation have also been filed against him, and gangster charges have been invoked multiple times. Kareli SHO Ashish Singh said the case would become clearer after Durrani’s arrest. Police scan 50+ cctv cameras Following the murder, police and forensic teams reached the spot and collected evidence. Investigators examined footage from more than 50 CCTV cameras in the area. Although the suspects were spotted in some clips, their identities could not be clearly established as their faces were covered. Post-mortem today The body has been sent for post-mortem, which will be conducted on Thursday. Irfan is survived by his wife Mangrul Nisha, two sons — Mohammad Aamir and Faisal — and two daughters. Family members gathered at the hospital, demanding answers over the killing.

stories.title: 'Now I have to support my national-level player daughter':Mother alleges son-in-law tried to hang daughter in Kashi
stories.summary: “Ask a mother. The daughter who once supported me, I have been supporting her for the last 10 months. She used to bring home medals. Today, I am asking for justice for her, which we have not received so far. Her husband left her to die and is now threatening us too.” These are the words of Nisha Singh, mother of national volleyball player Priya Singh, who is now unable to speak properly. Priya had topped her MP Ed from Kashi Vidyapeeth and was known for her achievements in sports. Condition worsens after alleged attack According to the family, the incident took place in July 2025. Nisha Singh alleges that Priya’s husband tried to kill her by hanging her with a noose. She survived, but lost her ability to speak and suffered memory loss. Since then, Priya has been dependent on her family for daily care. Her mother says her condition has not improved significantly. Mother approaches commissioner On 7 April, Nisha Singh reached Commissioner Mohit Agarwal with her daughter, seeking action in the case. She said the family has not received justice so far and is also facing threats. The Commissioner assured her that the matter would be looked into and that she would get justice. Family demands strict action Nisha Singh has demanded strict action against the accused. She says the delay in justice has added to their suffering. She also warned that if justice is not delivered, she may take an extreme step along with her daughter. Case raises serious questions The case highlights concerns over delays in action in serious assault cases and the safety of victims and their families after such incidents. Bhaskar spoke to Nisha Singh to understand how Priya’s condition worsened and what the family expects from the administration. First, take a look at Priya’s wedding photographs—moments filled with happiness and celebration. Then, see what followed… National volleyball player left speech-impaired, mother alleges attempt to murder; seeks action In a small house in Parmanandpur, Varanasi, medals and trophies line the walls—reminders of a sporting career that once brought pride to the family. Today, those same medals are silently watched by Priya Singh, a national volleyball player who can no longer speak properly or recall much of her past. Her mother, Nisha Singh, says their life changed months after Priya’s marriage. Marriage followed by alleged harassment According to Nisha, Priya was married on February 25, 2025, to Amit Kumar Verma, a junior engineer posted in Gorakhpur. The family claims they spent around ₹8 lakh on the wedding. Within a month, Priya allegedly began facing harassment. Nisha says her son-in-law pressured Priya to transfer family land in his name. When the family resisted, the harassment allegedly turned violent. July incident leaves Priya critical On July 8, 2025, at around 3 am, Nisha received a call from her in-laws claiming Priya had died by suicide in Gorakhpur. “When we reached, she was alive but critical,” Nisha said. Priya was first admitted to AIIMS Gorakhpur and later shifted to Lucknow and then to KGMU for specialised care. She remained in a coma for seven days and spent over three weeks in the ICU. Doctors found severe damage to her vocal cords, which has left her with difficulty in speaking. FIR filed, family alleges weak charges The family lodged a complaint at Shivpur police station in Varanasi on July 8. However, Nisha alleges that the case was registered under minor sections despite the seriousness of the incident. She claims no arrests have been made so far and alleges that the accused’s government position influenced the handling of the case. “From supporting us to needing support” Priya, who topped her M.P.Ed from Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith and captained its volleyball team, now struggles to speak even basic sentences. Sitting beside her medals, she tries to recall her achievements but often falls silent. Her mother says Priya cannot remember the day of the incident. “She was our support. Today, she needs support,” Nisha said. Police response SDCP Varuna Zone Neetu Kadyan said a case has been registered and the investigation is ongoing. “If any negligence is found, action will be taken. The culprits will not be spared,” she said. Family continues to seek justice Over the past months, Nisha says she has approached multiple officials, including senior police officers, but has not seen progress in the case. The family continues to demand stricter charges and immediate action, as Priya undergoes treatment and struggles to rebuild her life.

stories.title: UP farmer breaks down as hailstorm destroys crop:Hail blankets Hardoi, alert in 44 districts
stories.summary: A farmer in Hardoi broke down in tears after seeing his crop destroyed by rain and hail. Unseasonal storms, rain and hail continue to batter Uttar Pradesh. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 44 districts on Thursday, warning of strong winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph. While Lucknow and Varanasi saw clear skies with cool breezes, several other regions reported changing weather patterns. In Mathura, light fog was seen in rural areas on Thursday morning after days of rainfall. Cloud cover persisted across 10 western districts, including Agra, while parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh witnessed mild sunshine. In Hardoi, farmer Satiram was seen weeping inconsolably as he surveyed his damaged wheat crop. Showing his rain-soaked fields, he said, “Oh God, what do we do now?” On Wednesday evening, hailstorms hit six cities, including Bareilly and Meerut. In Saharanpur and Hardoi, heavy hail turned roads and fields white, resembling a blanket of snow. Over the past 24 hours, rainfall was recorded in 30 districts of the state. According to the weather department, the state received an average rainfall of 2.8 mm — nearly 200% above normal. The highest temperature in the state was recorded at 38.6°C in Banda. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh said the current western disturbance will weaken by Thursday, but a fresh system will become active from April 11. This could once again worsen weather conditions, bringing rain accompanied by strong winds and a drop in temperature by 6 to 8 degrees Celsius. Weather scenes from across Uttar Pradesh…

stories.title: 15 accused, multi-city kidney racket:Doctor brought surgical team from Meerut; Kanpur OT used for illicit surgeries
stories.summary: A large-scale illegal kidney transplant racket, originating from Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur, has exposed a well-organised network spanning nine hospitals across four cities in Uttar Pradesh. Investigations reveal that over 50 kidney transplants were carried out, with patients charged between ₹50 lakh and ₹2.5 crore. The racket came to light after a Bihar-based victim alleged he was underpaid for donating his kidney. Following the complaint, police cracked down on the network, arresting several individuals while others remain absconding. How the racket operated The network used agents, doctors, technicians, and hospital operators to identify donors and recipients. Poor and vulnerable individuals were lured through social media and messaging platforms, often with promises of ₹5–10 lakh. Illegal surgeries were conducted secretly, mostly between 3 am and 4 am, with hospital staff kept away and CCTV cameras switched off. The 15 key accused and their roles 1. Dr Preeti Ahuja Owner of Ahuja Hospital and one of the main accused. A qualified physician, she allegedly allowed her hospital to be used for illegal transplants. 2. Dr Surjit Singh Ahuja Her husband and co-operator of the hospital. He managed finances, coordinated doctors, and oversaw operations. 3. Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada An 8th-pass agent and key middleman. He identified donors and recipients through social media and arranged deals. 4. Dr Rohit (absconding) An anaesthesiologist who allegedly handled critical medical procedures and coordinated surgeries. 5. Dr Mudassir Ali Played a central role in surgeries, including removing and transplanting kidneys. 6. Dr Afzal Handled patient coordination and brought donors and recipients to Kanpur. 7. Dr Ram Prakash Kushwaha Operator of Medi Life Hospital, where patients were admitted before and after surgeries. 8. Dr Rajesh Kumar Associated with Medi Life Hospital; managed patient care and records. 9. Dr Narendra Singh alias Nandu Operator of Preeti Hospital, where patients were shifted post-surgery. 10. Parvez Saifi Driver and logistics handler who transported doctors, patients, and money. 11. Naveen Pandey (absconding) Allegedly linked to deal negotiations and pricing within the racket. 12. Kuldeep Singh Raghav OT technician who assisted in surgeries and coordinated with doctors. 13. Rajesh Kumar (OT technician) Experienced technician who assisted during operations for payment per case. 14. Dr Vaibhav A dentist whose role in transplant procedures is under investigation. 15. Amit alias Anurag (absconding) Linked to Alpha Hospital; suspected of coordinating with key doctors in the network. Expanding network across hospitals Investigators found that the racket extended beyond Ahuja Hospital, with links to Medi Life Hospital, Preeti Hospital, and Alpha Hospital in Meerut, among others. Patients were often moved between facilities to avoid suspicion. Police action so far Key concerns raised The case has raised serious questions about: What happens next Police are continuing raids to arrest absconding accused and trace financial links. Authorities are also examining whether more hospitals and medical professionals were involved.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court reshuffles 711 judicial officers:Maximum transfers across key UP districts, including 266 ADJs; see full list
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Sunday ordered the transfer of 266 Additional District and Sessions Judges. Registrar General Manjeet Singh Shyoran released the list, directing all officers to hand over charge by April 15 and take charge at their new postings. Several judge couples have been posted together. Santosh Kumar Yadav and Sandeepa Yadav have been moved from Azamgarh to Bareilly, while Vikas Nagar and Pratiksha Nagar have been transferred from Gautam Buddh Nagar to Gorakhpur. Gopal Ji and Machala Agrawal have been shifted from Bulandshahr to Sambhal, and Gaurav Sharma with Neetu Pathak from Ghaziabad to Varanasi. In another set of transfers, Nishant Yadav and Archana Yadav have been moved from Lucknow to Shahjahanpur, while Jyotna Sivach and Anurag Panwar have been transferred from Lucknow to Muzaffarnagar. Sita Ram and Alka Bharti have been posted from Muzaffarnagar to Rampur, and Manoj Kumar Sidhu with Garima Singh have also been shifted to Muzaffarnagar. Abhay Pratap Singh and Anuradha Pundir have been posted to Prayagraj from Shahjahanpur, while Manish Nigam and Poonam Dwitiya have been transferred from Unnao to Ghaziabad. Ajay Kumar and Parul Verma have been moved from Pratapgarh to Meerut. Several other couples have also been accommodated at the same locations. Special postings: Several judges have been assigned key roles in the High Court, Judicial Training and Research Institute (JTRI), Lucknow Bench, tribunals, and government departments. These include positions such as Registrar (Judicial), Additional Director at JTRI, Special Secretary, and Additional Law Officer. See the list... Maximum transfers across key UP districts: Agra, Aligarh, Bareilly, Gorakhpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj among most affected The Allahabad High Court administration carried out large-scale transfers across most districts of Uttar Pradesh, with Agra, Aligarh, Bareilly, Gorakhpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj, Kanpur Nagar, Varanasi, Meerut and Ghaziabad witnessing the highest movement of judicial officers. In total, 711 judicial officers were reshuffled on Sunday. This includes 266 Additional District and Sessions Judges, 169 Civil Judges (Senior Division), and 276 Civil Judges (Junior Division), marking one of the biggest administrative overhauls in recent times.

stories.title: Teen dies after drowning at temple pond:Playing on stairs before fall; NDRF recovers body, family protests
stories.summary: A 13-year-old boy died on Sunday after drowning in a pond built near the Karmdeshwar Mahadev Temple in Varanasi. The incident occurred when the boy was playing on the steps of the pond with his two friends. He lost balance and eventually landed in deep water. Local people said that even after two hours of hard effort when the boy was not found, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) was called, which found the boy Pawan Prajapati in 20 minutes, who had died due to drowning. When the police took possession of the body and tried to send it for post-mortem, there was an altercation with the family members and villagers, and the family members left with the body. They did not want a post-mortem. After the station in-charge explained, the family members agreed to the post-mortem. See four pictures related to the incident Three friends had come to play in afternoon A local resident said - In the afternoon, three friends reached the pond located near Karmdeshwar Mahadev temple. The steps of the pond here have moss on them. While slipping on it, Pawan Prajapati (13), a resident of Kandwa area, went into the deep pond. Seeing this, his companions started screaming and a crowd gathered, but by then Pawan had already submerged in the deep water. Police reached the spot and sent divers into the water to search for the teenager. Location could not be traced even after two hours of effort For two hours, divers kept searching for Pawan in Kandwa pond but could not find any trace of him. Meanwhile, on the banks of the pond, the family members were in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. The administration then informed the NDRF. After the NDRF divers arrived, they found Pawan within 20 minutes of effort, but by then Pawan had already died. Foam was coming out of his nose and mouth. Were not ready for post-mortem Seeing their son's body, the father, mother and other family members started wailing loudly. After this, when the police tried to take possession of the body, the family members refused the post-mortem. This led to a sharp argument between the police and the family members. The family members started walking towards home with the body, but the police stopped them midway, explained to them, and took possession of the body to send it for post-mortem.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Yogi Adityanath calls Syed Salar Masud a mafia figure; Modi says TMC sins will be accounted for after polls more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Modi says TMC sins will be accounted for after polls Addressing a rally at West Bengal's Cooch Behar, PM Modi accused the Trinamool Congress (TMC) of intimidation and corruption, urging people not to fear pressure on polling day and to trust the rule of law. 2. Yogi Adityanath calls Syed Salar Masud a mafia figure: Says, ‘Suheldev sent him to hell, punished him with Islam’s harshest death on hot griddle’ CM Yogi said in Lucknow on Sunday everyone should know the valour shown by Maharaja Suheldev a thousand years ago. He not only stopped the foreign invader who broke the Somnath temple but also gave him such a brutal death that no one dared repeat it. 3. Shankaracharya targets Mohan Bhagwat with a remark: Questions his marriage and children, says support will go to those who listen We had said that Mohan Bhagwat and his propagandists should come, get married, have children, and increase the population. On one hand, the government is saying that there is a population explosion. On the other hand, these people talk about increasing the population. If increasing the population is so important, then why don't you get married and have children? Why do you burden others? Do it yourself first, then tell others. 4. PAK minister Khawaja Asif threatens India Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif, speaking to journalists in Sialkot, threatened India. He said that, unlike last year, India will face even greater embarrassment this time. 5. Former Lok Sabha Speaker recalls facing untouchability in Lucknow: Says the leader invited her for breakfast, the woman inside objected using a caste remark I have also faced untouchability. My mother also suffered during her studies, and my father could not escape it even while holding a top political position. This is what Meira Kumar, who was the Speaker of the Lok Sabha during the Congress rule, said. 6. Mastermind in Kanpur kidney scam claims huge money: Audio recording with agent recovered, Kannauj doctor caught Police have found an audio recording from the mobile phone of Shivam Agarwal, the mastermind of Kanpur's infamous kidney scam. According to DCP West SM Qasim Abidi, he had sent this recording to Naveen Pandey, a resident of Prayagraj, who was part of the gang. 7. Trump says wounded F-15 crew member rescued from Iran US President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that a seriously wounded but “very brave” F-15 crew member has been rescued from deep inside the mountains of Iran. 8. 4 suspects arrested in Lucknow after ATS probe: Pakistan handler Abu Bakar paid ₹12K per arson Four suspected terrorists were arrested in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. During ATS questioning, it came out that they had an offer from Pakistan to spread terror for money. The suspects were told the more fear they created, the more money they would get. 9. Family cuts ties with burqa-clad robbery accused woman: Father-in-law says ‘we are ashamed’; house locked in Ayodhya, family in Punjab This is what Hariram, the father-in-law of Payal (25), the woman who robbed a jewellery shop in Ayodhya wearing a burqa, said. He works and lives in Punjab. When asked about his daughter-in-law, he expressed displeasure. 10 IPL's valuation equals 95% of India's entire sports industry Citing a report by Kotak Mutual Fund, news agency ANI says the IPL is now worth around $18 billion (₹1.69 lakh crore). That's similar to the economic size of numerous small countries.

stories.title: Sunanda Sharma forgives student who rushed stage in Ghaziabad:Fan apologises after scare; singer urges leniency from authorities
stories.summary: A student from Rajkumar Goel Institute of Technology (RKGIT), Ghaziabad, who ran onto the stage to approach Punjabi singer Sunanda Sharma on April 3, has issued a public apology. On Sunday, he was seen holding his ears—a common gesture of remorse—while asking for forgiveness. Identifying himself as Shivang Pandey, the student said he is a devoted fan and acted impulsively while the singer was performing. “I suddenly went on stage to touch her feet. I apologize… If you forgive me, the college management will also forgive me,” he said. Singer responds, urges leniency Sunanda Sharma also shared a video on Instagram addressing the incident. She confirmed that she has forgiven the student and appealed to the college administration to take a softer approach. She acknowledged that while fans often express admiration in different ways, such actions can be alarming. “What the student did frightened me, especially given the kind of incidents happening with performers these days,” she said. The singer added that she had no prior indication of the student’s sudden arrival on stage. She admitted feeling scared at the moment, which led to a strong reaction, and said she briefly left the stage due to security concerns. Appeal for understanding and responsible behaviour Sunanda emphasized that while the student’s intentions may not have been harmful, the manner of expression was inappropriate. She urged authorities not to punish him harshly, stating that since she has forgiven him, the administration should also consider doing the same. She also advised fans to express admiration in a respectful way that does not inconvenience or endanger others. Thanking her supporters, she credited her success to their continued love and encouragement. Student reiterates apology In a separate video, Shivang again apologised directly to the singer. “My intention was not wrong. I did not mean to hurt you. I hope you forgive me so the college management will also forgive me,” he said. What happened on stage Student breaches security During the performance, while Sunanda was engaging the audience, students were recording videos and taking selfies near the stage. Amid this, Shivang managed to bypass security and climbed onto the stage unnoticed. Singer startled as student approaches He quickly moved towards the singer and attempted to touch her feet, which startled her. Sunanda screamed in fear, prompting immediate intervention from security personnel, who escorted her away. Brief disruption before removal Following the incident, the student remained on stage momentarily, even striking a pose with arms spread, before security and police intervened. He was eventually removed and taken into custody for questioning. Show cancelled after incident The disruption led to the event being called off due to security concerns. Sunanda Sharma left the venue and did not return to continue the performance, despite repeated requests from students.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath calls Syed Salar Masud a mafia figure:Says, 'Suheldev sent him to hell, punished him with Islam’s harshest death on hot griddle'
stories.summary: CM Yogi said in Lucknow on Sunday everyone should know the valour shown by Maharaja Suheldev a thousand years ago. He not only stopped the foreign invader who broke the Somnath temple but also gave him such a brutal death that no one dared repeat it. Yogi said, “Salar Masud (Ghazi Mian) was no less than a mafia. He was like the mafias who have now been reduced to dust. He had broken our temples. Maharaja Suheldev gave him a death considered the worst in Islam. He was tied to a hot iron griddle and burned.” Yogi said—it is believed that such a death in Islam guarantees going to hell. Maharaja Suheldev ensured he would go to hell. Until we treat oppressors in this manner, they will continue to treat India's culture the same way. Yogi was speaking at the inauguration of the Golden Jubilee Drama Festival marking 50 years of the Bharatendu Natya Academy (BNA). He inaugurated the academy building and two auditoriums, honoured artists and students, and released the magazine ‘Rangbhed’. See Photos- 3. Where Salar Masood was killed, a fair was held in his name Yogi said- Indian society had forgotten Maharaja Suheldev. Our government built his memorial. If this is not slavery, then what is it? At the place where the Maharaja killed Salar Masood, a Masood fair used to be held. There was no mention of Suheldev. The Maharaja's contribution was not remembered by anyone. But now people visit Maharaja Suheldev's memorial. 4. 'Organized a program for Maharaja Suheldev while being an MP from Gorakhpur' The CM said that when I was an MP from Gorakhpur. We had organized a program in Bahraich on the Vijayotsav (victory celebration) of Maharaja Suheldev. When I was going there, the administration tried to stop me. But, I still went. At that time, there wasn't much crowd at the event. A large number of people were going to Salar Masood's fair. Why were they going to the fair of someone who came to crush them? But, now times have changed. Today I feel good. The crowd now goes to Maharaja Suheldev's memorial instead. No one even peeks into Salar Masood's fair. 5. 'Those who trampled India's culture should not be honored' The CM said - There is no play, no music on Maharaja Suheldev. We should create something on them. Music and plays should be made on Veerangana Avantibai, Veerangana Udadevi, Veerangana Jhalkaribai, Maharaja Bijli Pasi. The Drama Academy should create short plays. So that children will consider them their heroes. The villains who trampled India's culture should never be honored. The story of Maharaja Suheldev Maharaja Suheldev was born in Shravasti in 990 AD. According to Mirat-e-Masoodi, a Persian language text written in the 17th century, Suheldev was the eldest son of King Mordhwaj of Shravasti. In various versions of legends, he is known by different names including Sakardev, Suhiradhwaj, Suhridil, Suhridaladhwaj, Rai Suhrid Dev, Susaj, and Suhardal. According to the Awadh Gazetteer, his reign lasted from 1027 to 1077 AD. His kingdom was mainly spread across Bahraich and Shravasti districts, with its expansion said to have extended to Gorakhpur in the east and Sitapur in the west. Parmeshwar Singh, former spokesperson of KV Inter College Payagpur, Bahraich, had provided detailed information about Maharaja Suheldev 8 years ago. According to him, about 3 kilometers north of Bahraich city, there was a huge Suryakund (sun pond) and a grand Sun Temple. A Mahatma named Balark Rishi lived there. He was the guru of Maharaja Suheldev. Suheldev had special proficiency in archery, firing sound-piercing arrows, swordsmanship, mace, and spear throwing. He also had a passion for swimming in the river. Hunting lions with arrows and swords was a common thing for him. As per the Guru's command, no woman other than his mother could come near him until the age of 25. He was a ruler of high caliber. During his time, people did not feel the need to lock their houses. He gave a beautiful form to the city of Shravasti. Maharaja Suheldev's Memorial Built by the Lake Chittaura Lake is located 8 km from Bahraich district headquarters on Gonda Road. A memorial to Maharaja Suheldev has been built on the banks of the lake. A 40-foot-high bronze statue of Maharaja Suheldev has been installed here. It is claimed that this statue is the country's largest statue of Maharaja Suheldev riding a horse standing on two legs. This statue was constructed under the supervision of the Uttar Pradesh State Lalit Kala Akademi. It was created by sculptor Padma Shri Ram Sutar. stories.title: Former Lok Sabha Speaker recalls facing untouchability in Lucknow:Says leader invited her for breakfast, woman inside objected using caste remark
stories.summary: I have also faced untouchabilitymy mother also suffered during her studies, and my father could not escape it even while holding a top political position. This is what Meira Kumar, who was the Speaker of the Lok Sabha during the Congress rule, said. At the Samta Diwas program organized in Lucknow on the birth anniversary of her father Babu Jagjivan Ram, she said- When my mother went to college after completing her school education, she was told that they would not teach an untouchable. A leader invited me for breakfast. From inside, a woman said that if they fed these untouchables, they would have to break the plate. Read the highlights of Meira Kumar's address 'Mother faced untouchability in Lucknow' Meira Kumar said, My maternal grandparents' home is in Kanpur. My maternal grandfather, Dr. Veerbal, was a very prominent doctor in Kanpur. In 1911, when the plague spread, everyone fled, but he did not. He would have lime put in wells, arrange for the burial of the dead, and treat those who survived. My mother, Indrani Devi, completed her schooling in Kanpur. After completing her schooling, when she went to college, she was told - 'We will not educate the daughter of an untouchable.' My father sent her to Lucknow. My mother completed her higher education here, staying in a hostel for 4 years, but even here, she was treated with untouchability. 'Even being in Congress, I couldn't escape untouchability' Meira Kumar said- I am Babu Ji's daughter, I was in the Foreign Service. I have been in Congress for so long, yet I couldn't escape it. I went to Chennai. There, a leader invited me for breakfast at his house. There were 4 other people with me. When we arrived, some voices were coming from inside. The people with me stood up and said, "Sister, let's go from here, we won't stay here for even a minute." Inside, a woman was saying that all untouchables are sitting. After feeding them, we will have to break all the plates. We will not eat. I said, 'Sit down, and if you don't listen to restrictions elsewhere, then eat here. If someone is inviting you with so much love and feeding you dosa, halwa, idli, sambar, then eat it. They will break their own plates, why are you worrying?' The 1978 Banaras Incident and the Reply of Ravidas Temple Referring to the incident of January 24, 1978, Meira Kumar said - Babu Ji was invited to Banaras for the unveiling of Sampurnanand's statue. During the unveiling, there was insulting behavior and slogans were raised in protest. He quietly returned. This was debated in the Rajya Sabha-Parliament. A condemnation motion was passed. But my Babu Ji did not say anything. My mother also asked why he was not saying anything? A year later in 1979, my father told mother that he had thought of a reply to the Banaras incident. Mother was surprised that he thought of a reply after a year. Then she asked back what reply he had thought of. Father replied - I have bought land on the banks of the Ganga, I will build a very large Ravidas temple there. This is my offering in return for what Banaras gave me. Referring to the temple, he said - In this temple, high ideals are worshipped. The sayings of great saints are inscribed on marble. In all four corners, symbols of different religions - temple, mosque, church, Buddhist monastery - are all built. Babuji backed down in honor of women Meira Kumar said that after independence, a movement began for the entry of women into temples. Regarding this, Babuji was leading the Temple Liberation Movement. He was opening temples for women with harmony. Babuji also reached Banaras to open the Kashi Vishwanath Temple for women. Some people were protesting. However, their number was very small. Early in the morning, Babuji received a call asking what to do? The protesters had laid down women from their homes in the alleys leading to the temple. We cannot go by stepping over them. Babuji said that respecting women is greater than seeing God, come back. 'There is still much to be done' In the end, Meira Kumar asked the assembly - There is still trouble, pain is caused. Wherever I go, I ask my Dalit brothers - Has untouchability ended? They say yes, we have separated the handpump. There is still much to be done. Appealing to the pioneers and young workers of Congress, she said, 'You move forward. Bring revolution. Change society. My truth is not sweet, it is bitter.' She asked the assembly - Will you fight this unfinished battle?" Hearing the echo of 'yes' from the crowd, she said, Then this will be a true tribute to Babu Ji.

stories.title: Shankaracharya asks why Mohan Bhagwat doesn’t marry and have children:Says we will stand with whoever listens to us
stories.summary: We had said that Mohan Bhagwat and his propagandists should come, get married, have children, and increase the population. On one hand, the government is saying that there is a population explosion. On the other hand, these people talk about increasing the population. If increasing the population is so important, then why don't you get married and have children? Why do you burden others? Do it yourself first, then tell others. Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati said these things during a press conference in Bareilly on Sunday. He was responding to a question related to the RSS chief's statement about having 3 children. In fact, Bhagwat has said many times that it is necessary for Hindus to have three children. Last month, during his visit to Mathura, Bhagwat had also said - Doctors believe that if a family has three children, the chances of parents and children being healthy increase. As psychology states, when there are three children in a home, they grow up to develop better and balanced personalities. Mutual quarrels and conflicts also decrease. On the question of supporting the opposition, Shankaracharya said that the ruling party says that we are with the opposition. I want to tell them to listen to us. Make laws for the protection of mother cow. We will stand with you. I am not with any party or opposition. Whoever listens to us, I will stand with them. 'I am surprised to see scholars silent on the America-Israel war' During a press conference at Devbhoomi Industrial Training Institute, Swami Avimukteshwaranand said - When there is a war, there are always two sides, one of justice and the other of injustice. For example, today one side is America and Israel, and the other is Iran. It is surprising that scholars all over the world are silent on this issue. This is a crime against humanity. Shankaracharya said, what was Prime Minister Narendra Modi's reaction to the war. On this, I would not like to say anything, but it is the duty of a scholar to state that this person is committing injustice and this person is suffering injustice, because in war, both sides cannot be good. He said - India has been a non-aligned country from the beginning. India has never stood with anyone in war. This is the first time, due to the Prime Minister's silence, the question is arising in people's minds that he might be standing on someone's side. Shankaracharya said that the Prime Minister is openly in favor of the Jews. This puts us in a state of worry. Is India falling into the trap of the Jews? Due to the war, there is a shortage of gas cylinders, but the Prime Minister and Chief Minister are not aware of this, because there is no power cut at their residences. Nor is there any shortage of rations. For them, everything is fine, but the public is distressed. 'Vote on the issue of cow protection' Shankaracharya said that I had given the government a deadline to bring a law on the issue of cow protection, but my words were not heard. I would urge opposition leaders to inspire people to vote on the issue of cow protection. I would like to tell the public to vote on the issue of cow protection. He said that as soon as elections approach, issues like 'Love Jihad' and religious conversion will be brought forward to divert attention, but the public should not be diverted. They should only vote on their own issues. In Hinduism, the cow (Go-Mata) holds great importance. Whenever bread (roti) is made in Hindu homes, the first bread is offered to the cow. 'Going to Rishikesh, came to Bareilly at the committee's request' Shankaracharya said - We are traveling from Varanasi, via Delhi, to Rishikesh. The summer doors of Lord Badrinath are about to open. For that, according to tradition, the pot of sacred oil has arrived in Rishikesh from the royal family. Now, from Rishikesh, it will be dispatched on April 8 for Badrinath Ji, via Jyotirmath. This is a tradition. He informed - This time, the committee had requested us to come. We are going for that. While traveling, it occurred to us that Bareilly is a city of religion. The way the scholars here have always connected people to Sanatan Dharma. We like that. That's why we have stopped in Bareilly.

stories.title: Family cuts ties with burqa-clad robbery accused woman:Father-in-law says ‘we are ashamed’; house locked in Ayodhya, family in Punjab
stories.summary: 'We had no idea that our daughter-in-law could do something like this. She has shamed us. Now there is no relationship with her; we will not bring her home.' This is what Hariram, the father-in-law of Payal (25), the woman who robbed a jewellery shop in Ayodhya wearing a burqa, said. He works and lives in Punjab. When asked about his daughter-in-law, he expressed displeasure. He said that after his son went to work, Payal would leave the house without informing anyone. She would remain missing for hours. When questioned, she would start arguing back. She would talk on the phone for a long time, but it was not clear with whom she was speaking. Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Payal's in-laws' house, where they found it locked. The father-in-law provided several important pieces of information about Payal during a phone conversation. Married a year ago, stayed together for a short time Bhaskar's team reached Subba village, Kotia, Payal's in-laws' house. The house was locked. Villagers said that all family members live in Punjab. They do labor and tailoring work. No one in the village had any inkling of this incident. The father-in-law is a mason by profession. We got the number of Payal's father-in-law, Hariram, from the villagers. In a phone conversation, Hariram said - Payal was married to his son Deepu last April. Deepu works as a tailor with his elder brother in Moga, Punjab. After marriage, Payal could only stay at her in-laws' house for a very short time, about 3 months. Illness and controversies were discussed Whenever Payal came to Punjab, she often complained of being ill, but as soon as she went to her maternal home, she would get well. Her behavior was not normal in her in-laws' house, and she used to constantly argue with her elder sister-in-law over small matters. See Payal's pictures Good behaviour with husband and children After the incident, there are various discussions in the village, but no one is openly willing to say anything. The father-in-law says that Payal's behavior with her husband was good. She used to cook food on time and her attitude towards the children of the house was also fine. She had come to her maternal home in Ayodhya, Mathana Nivada's Ahibaran Ka Purwa village, to take her intermediate examination on March 16. Read the full story in detail Arrived wearing a burqa to buy a gold necklace-chain Mahesh, a jeweler, resides in Kothi Bazar Mohalla of Rudauli area. His shop, named Mahesh Jewelers, is located in Agarwal Complex, 900 meters away from his home. On April 2, Thursday afternoon, a girl wearing a burqa arrived at the shop. She had a backpack. The girl said, "I want to buy a gold necklace and chain." Mahesh showed her a gold necklace and chain. During this, the girl asked for water. Mahesh sent Ankit, who works in the shop, to bring water and samosa. When Ankit brought the samosa and water, Payal refused to eat. She said, "I don't eat samosas. Please order sweets." Mahesh sent Ankit to get barfi. During this, the shop employee Maniram picked up the necklace and chain and placed them on the counter. Then the girl stood up and started wandering around inside the shop. Mahesh asked - What's the matter? The girl replied - My husband went to withdraw money, he hasn't returned, I'm just looking for him. Then she came and stood near the counter. Mahesh started putting other jewelry in the cupboard, just then Payal picked up the gold necklace and chain kept in the box. She picked up her bag. Showing a pistol, she said - I will shoot you. When shopkeeper Mahesh interrupted, she pulled out a pistol from her waist. Pointing it at Mahesh, she said, 'If you move forward, I will shoot you.' After that, she ran out of the shop. Mahesh and Maniram chased her, shouting. She ran out of the shop on foot and fled with a young man who was waiting on a bike a short distance away. Mahesh said that the jewellery was 26 grams (22 carat). According to the market price on April 2, its value was approximately 3 lakh 60 thousand rupees. Mahesh immediately informed the police. 60 CCTV footage was extracted, then the vehicle number was found The daylight robbery caused a stir in the police. Police formed 5 teams and started the investigation. 60 CCTV cameras in the vicinity were scanned. The footage showed that the girl left on a motorcycle with a young man. The bike's number was extracted, through which the location was traced. Police first reached Paran Ka Purwa. There, Rahul was identified. Police arrested Rahul. During interrogation, Rahul revealed that a girl named Payal was also with him. After this, Payal was arrested the same night from Ahibaran Ka Purwa village in Mathana Nivada. Police, while revealing the incident, recovered the stolen jewelry and a fake pistol. Both accused have been arrested and sent to jail. Rahul was unemployed, used to visit Payal's village Rahul's family, a resident of Paran Ka Purwa, is economically weak. His father Radheshyam has passed away. He is the youngest of 3 brothers. Elder brother Lavkush stays at home. One brother, Bablu, works as a laborer in Delhi. Rahul lives separately with his mother but does no work. The distance from Payal's house to his house is about 16 km. They came into contact due to his frequent visits to the village.

stories.title: Mastermind in Kanpur kidney scam claims huge money:Audio recording with agent recovered, Kannauj doctor caught
stories.summary: Police have found an audio recording from the mobile phone of Shivam Agarwal, the mastermind of Kanpur's infamous kidney scam. According to DCP West SM Qasim Abidi, he had sent this recording to Naveen Pandey, a resident of Prayagraj, who was part of the gang. In the audio, Naveen is mentioning Sahil, a broker from Prayagraj, to Shivam. He says that Sahil has taken 22 lakh rupees using your name. To this, Shivam says - he doesn't know what Shivam and Dr. Rohit are, we just throw away crores of rupees like that. Meanwhile, the police team reached Naveen Pandey's house in Prayagraj on Saturday evening, but he was not found. Meanwhile, the police called Shivam's wife to Rawatpur police station for questioning. She stated that Naveen has been working with Dr. Rohit, a resident of Ghaziabad, for 4-5 years. Shivam had only been associated with Dr. Rohit for one year. Police will file a petition in the district court on Monday, seeking Shivam's remand. According to the police, this recording is from December last year. However, the police have not made it public. So far, 9 people have been arrested in the kidney scam. Kannauj Doctor Detained by Police According to the police, Shivam is mentioning a woman in the recording. He says that the woman we brought to Delhi, who was admitted to Max Hospital in Dwarka, died. To this, Naveen says that the woman should have been taken by ambulance, but you people took her in a Scorpio. Does a Scorpio have any medical facilities? According to the police, the woman mentioned in the audio underwent a kidney transplant at Medilife Hospital in December. After this, her health deteriorated. She was immediately admitted to Max Hospital in Delhi, where she died. Police have taken Dr. Rohan, a resident of Kannauj, into custody on Saturday in connection with the woman's death. He is being interrogated. The hospital's two other partners, Dr. Narendra, a resident of Auraiya, and Dr. Sandeep from Kannauj, are currently absconding. Sahil defrauded 20 lakh in the name of kidney Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said that like Shivam Agarwal, Sahil also worked for Dr. Rohit. The investigation revealed that a woman needed a kidney. Sahil contacted her and said that Dr. Rohit charges 40 lakh for a transplant, but he would arrange a kidney transplant for 20 lakh rupees. After this, he took 20 lakh rupees from the woman and absconded. The Police Commissioner said that raids are being conducted in Chitrakoot and Prayagraj in search of Sahil. So far, none of the doctors whose names have come forward in the gang are surgeons. The gang includes Dr. Rohit, an anesthesiologist, Dr. Vaibhav, a dentist, Dr. Anurag, Alpha Hospital operator, Dr. Afzal, a physician, and Dr. Ali, an OT technician. BA pass Bhupendra became a Doctor of Medicine The DCP said that Shivam's wife was interrogated for about 6 hours on Friday. During this, she named Bhupendra Singh, the manager of Ramashiv Hospital located opposite Hallet. Bhupendra Singh was in contact with Dr. Rohit. When the police interrogated him, he revealed that he had built a private hospital in Lucknow, opposite SGPGI. According to DCP West, Bhupendra's visiting card had MD (Doctor of Medicine) written on it. When asked, he stated that MD stands for Managing Director. He was in contact with Dr. Rohit. Dr. Rohit had asked him to get a kidney transplant done at his hospital, but he did not undergo the transplant. The operators of Medilife, Rohan, Narendra, and Ajay, are also being interrogated. Meerut's travel agent used to book cars under fake names Dr. Anurag alias Amit had two marriages The police team reached Meerut in search of Dr. Anurag, who is linked to the scandal. The investigation revealed that Meerut's Alpha Hospital is in Dr. Anurag's name. He is a physiotherapist and has married twice. The police team reached his first wife's house, but he was not found there. The police are searching for his second wife's location. Now know the connection to Medilife Hospital DCP Abidi stated that OT technicians Rajesh Kumar and Kuldeep Singh Raghav had said during interrogation that they had performed all operations at Ahuja Hospital, but an examination of their mobile phones revealed numbers of several other hospitals in the city. This includes Medilife Hospital located in Maswanpur.

stories.title: Fake note mastermind’s political ties questioned:BJP MLA attended event, SP flags found in his house and vehicle
stories.summary: Politics has erupted over Vivek Yadav, the mastermind behind fake notes in UP. BJP leaders are calling him a Samajwadi, while SP leaders are proving the accused to be a BJP member. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav targeted BJP MLA Shalabhmani from Deoria. Asked - When will he be interrogated? How far is Deoria from Gorakhpur? Pictures of Vivek Yadav with Shalabhmani were also posted. On the other hand, Shalabhmani and other BJP members are posting pictures on social media to prove Vivek is an SP leader. After Vivek's name came up in the fake currency case, leaders of both parties are also distancing themselves. The question arises, which party is Vivek Yadav from Deoria actually associated with? Read this in Sunday Big Story Photo with MLA, Samajwadi Party said - Vivek belongs to BJP This case began with the action of Deoria police on April 30. Two boys each from Bhadohi and Deoria were caught with fake notes worth 1.80 lakh rupees. These boys worked for Vivek Yadav of Deoria. It came to light that fake notes of 500, 200, and 100 rupees were being printed in Deoria and spread across Uttar Pradesh. As soon as Vivek Yadav's name came up in this case, local BJP leaders in Deoria became active on social media. Vivek's pictures were posted with captions saying that he is a 'Sapayi' (SP supporter)... he campaigns for SP. Like Atiq in the film 'Dhurandhar', he was circulating fake notes in UP. This is where politics began in the entire matter. On April 1, the SP media cell shared 4 pictures. In these, the arrested boys were seen with MLA Shalabhmani. The post asked why there are pictures of these boys with MLA Shalabhmani. The BJP and the government's administration are making a hue and cry about these boys who were circulating fake notes, will BJP leaders explain what these boys were doing with Shalabhmani? Will Shalabhmani be questioned in the fake notes case? Akhilesh asked - Why the delay in action? After SP's X handle, party chief Akhilesh Yadav also wrote on social media- Pictures of those circulating fake notes have been found with a BJP MLA, from the street to his office, as evidence. Then why the delay in taking action against them? Bhaskar spoke to Deoria's BJP MLA Shalabhmani Tripathi Question. Did you attend Vivek Yadav's event? Your photo with him has surfaced. Shalabhamani. I am the MLA here; every day in the morning, people come to us and present their issues. One day, Vivek Yadav came to invite us to a program related to the installation of the idol of Kali Maa in his village. He also took a photo with me. We attended that program. In these programs, we don't look at who belongs to SP or who belongs to BJP. We always reach out to people. Question. Is Vivek a supporter of BJP or SP? Shalabhamani. Look at Vivek's complete profile, and you will clearly see that he is associated with SP. Despite this, Akhilesh Yadav is linking him to BJP, whereas at such a time, he should have explained to his workers to stay away from such activities. Work for the party. But he is washing his hands of the matter by calling his own worker a member of another party. Deoria SP District President said - Vivek has no position in the party To understand Vivek Yadav's political affiliation more closely, Bhaskar also spoke to Vyas Yadav, the SP District President of Deoria. We asked - Does Vivek hold any position in the SP? He says - this person is neither an office bearer of SP nor a general worker. He has no association with the party at any level. All this appears to be a well-thought-out conspiracy to tarnish the image of SP. The accused is associated with some influential leaders of other political parties, but those people are linking the accused to SP out of political malice, which is absolutely wrong.

stories.title: 4 suspects arrested in Lucknow after ATS probe:Pakistan handler Abu Bakar paid ₹12K per arson
stories.summary: Four suspected terrorists were arrested in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. During ATS questioning, it came out they had an offer from Pakistan to spread terror for money. The suspects were told the more fear they created, the more money they would get. To plan a big blast, they carried out a rehearsal by setting a pickup truck and a bike on fire. They sent videos of these acts to a Pakistani handler, Abu Bakar, and received 12 thousand rupees for each arson. On Saturday, all four accused were presented before a special court in Lucknow. UP ATS was granted 5-day remand of Shakib, Vikas Gehlawat, Lokesh alias Papla Pandit, and Arbab. During this period, ATS will interrogate them about the tasks given by the Pakistani handler. AK-47 belongs to Akib of Dubai ADG Law and Order Amitabh Yash says, ‘This is a sensitive matter. The age group of these boys is between 19 and 27 years. These boys are masters in Google search, they gather information by searching for material very quickly. Among the four boys, Saqib was giving directions to everyone.’ He was getting help from his brother Akib in Dubai. Saqib told ATS that the AK-47 he is holding in the photo, belongs to his brother Akib, who lives in Dubai. Several pictures of Akib with an AK-47 have also been found. Now ATS is trying to find out where Akib got this AK-47 from. Many videos of arson, location and timing being ascertained So far, the investigation has revealed that these people had set fire to a pickup truck and made videos of it a month ago on March 4. This arson took place in the Kiratpur area. Seven mobile phones found with the four boys contained more such videos, and we are currently checking their locations to determine when and where these incidents occurred. Burnt vehicles are not investigated, they took advantage of this Amitabh Yash says, ‘Records of arson incidents in vehicles, shops, and small establishments in the districts of Bulandshahr, Bijnor, Meerut, Baghpat, Hapur in West UP over the last 6 months are being reviewed to ascertain what connection these four have with these incidents. Investigating agencies believe that these boys were doing this because vehicles have insurance, and after burning them, they were not investigated much.’ They contacted Pakistan in 2 ways, most numbers from Afghanistan Amitabh Yash said, ‘During the investigation, it also came to light that these people contacted Abu Bakar of Pakistan in 2 ways.’ 1. They used the Signal app for calling. 2. They used Instagram to send documents and video files. They used VPN so they wouldn't get caught. This is why, when tracing IP addresses, most numbers appear to be from Afghanistan's location. Found in YouTube's search history - how to make a chemical bomb In the YouTube search history of Shakib and Arbab's mobiles, it was found: how to make a time bomb, how to make a chemical bomb, and what are the techniques for accurate targeting? They have also watched many videos, and Abu Bakar sent them some links and videos. How much these people were able to learn will only become clear after 5 days of remand. Videos of military bases were made and sent to Pakistan Interrogation of the arrested suspected terrorists revealed that they had collected information about military bases in UP. Videos of the cantonment areas were prepared. This information was also sent to Pakistan. It is being said that Hindu leaders of UP were also on their target. The suspected terrorists had also gathered information about their movements. How did ATS reach these four boys? ATS sources say - On March 4, 2026, Nimish Rastogi's pickup van was set on fire in Bijnor. Police arrested Abuzar and Zaid in connection with it on March 12. According to the police, Abuzar was struggling with financial difficulties. He sought help from his cousin Mohammad Zaid. Zaid connected him to Abu Bakar via the Telegram app. Abu Bakar gave directions to set Hindu vehicles on fire. After this, Abuzar set fire to the van near the temple, recorded a video of the incident, and sent it to Abu Bakar via Telegram. After this, money was transferred to his account. Evidence was found that Zaid was connected to 12 different groups. Both UP ATS and NIA are investigating this matter. During this investigation, Saqib's links to Abubakar were also found, after which ATS put Saqib's mobile number under surveillance and started tracking him.

stories.title: 11 dead in Vrindavan boat mishap:Who are the 4 people responsible? No lifejackets, allegations of overcrowding boat
stories.summary: A boat carrying devotees capsized in Vrindavan after colliding with a pontoon bridge on the Yamuna river. So far, 11 people have died, while five are still missing. Just 15 minutes before the accident, passengers were seen laughing and enjoying the ride. Within minutes, the situation turned tragic. No life jackets, overcrowding alleged The boat was carrying 37 passengers in water nearly 25–30 feet deep. None of them were given life jackets. Strong winds of around 30–40 kmph were blowing, but the operator did not slow down or stop despite repeated warnings from passengers. Experts say many lives could have been saved if life jackets were provided. How the accident unfolded The boat was around 50 feet from the shore when it started shaking due to strong winds. Passengers warned the boatman as the pontoon bridge approached, but he did not stop. After avoiding collision twice, the boat hit the bridge on the third attempt. The impact caused passengers to fall to one side, and the boat capsized. Boat operator’s role under question The boat operator, Pappu Nishad, allegedly ignored basic safety rules: After the accident, he fled the spot. Contractor’s lapse flagged The pontoon bridge was being dismantled under a riverfront project. Contractor Narayan Sharma allegedly: This allowed boats to enter a risky area. Civic body under scrutiny The Municipal Corporation is responsible for issuing licences and ensuring safety. However: The boat involved in the accident was also unlicensed. Administration’s failure The local administration is responsible for safety at ghats and monitoring boating. But: Officials are now facing serious questions. Legal action and investigation Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against the boat owner and contractor. However, there is debate over whether stricter charges should be applied due to serious negligence. Safety rules in place Guidelines in Uttar Pradesh require: Family tragedy: 7 relatives among dead Seven members of one family died in the accident. The victims include Madhur Bahal, his mother Kavita Bahal, Charanjit, Pinky Bahal, Asha Rani, Anju Gulati and Rakesh Gulati.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:11 dead in Vrindavan boat tragedy; JD Vance meets Pak PM ahead of US-Iran ceasefire talks more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. JD Vance meets Pak PM ahead of US-Iran ceasefire talks US Vice President J D Vance is holding talks with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ahead of the ceasefire talks between Iran and the United States. 2. Vrindavan boat tragedy: toll rises to 11, massive Yamuna search underway Death toll in the Vrindavan boat tragedy has risen to 11, with 4 still missing. Around 250 divers are combing a 14-km stretch of the Yamuna river. The ferry owner has been detained as rescue operations intensify. 3. Mirzapur lawyer shot dead during morning walk, CCTV captures attack A lawyer was shot dead in Mirzapur during a morning walk as two bike-borne assailants fired at close range and fled. CCTV captured the incident. Locals were threatened at gunpoint when they tried to chase the attackers. Police suspect election rivalry behind the killing. 4. PM Modi calls Mamata govt ‘nirmam sarkar’: Promises 8th Pay Commission benefits Speaking in West Bengal's Purba Bardhaman, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Bengal is ready for change, adding that his “Modi guarantee” is to replace the fear under the Trinamool Congress’s “ruthless rule” with trust. 5. Meerut shocker: father kept daughter’s corpse for 4 months, used perfume to mask stench A disturbing case has emerged in Meerut where a father lived with his daughter’s decomposed body for four months. The teacher had died of jaundice. He allegedly used perfume to hide the smell until relatives alerted police, who recovered the skeletal remains. 6. Rohini Ghawari backs SP, plans 200 meetings to mobilise Dalits in UP Dr Rohini Ghawari, former partner of Chandrashekhar Azad, has decided to support Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh. She plans 200 meetings targeting non-Jatav Dalits and will return from Switzerland in June, aiming to build a new social base for the Samajwadi Party. 7. EC drops 6.08 crore voters in 12 states/UTs during SIR The Election Commission of India has released the final voter list under the second phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, leading to the removal of more than 6.08 crore names from electoral rolls across nine states and three Union Territories. 8. Yogi renames Miyanpur to Rabindranagar, land rights to Bangladeshi Hindus Yogi Adityanath announced renaming Miyanpur village in Lakhimpur Kheri as Rabindranagar, invoking Rabindranath Tagore. He also distributed land ownership rights to Bangladeshi Hindu families and launched multiple development projects during his visit. 9. Dubai–Kathmandu flight makes emergency landing in Lucknow, resumes after 90 minutes A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Kathmandu made an emergency landing at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport due to bad weather. The aircraft, carrying 154 passengers, landed safely, underwent checks and refuelling, and departed again after about 90 minutes. 10. 'Women's reservation bill shouldn't be a political tool':Tharoor warns rushing delimitation Congress leader Shashi Tharoor said that amendments to be made in the Women's Reservation Bill should not be used as a political weapon, so that federalism is not weakened and the dignity of Parliament is not hurt.

stories.title: Chaos erupts during Akshay Kumar's film promotion:Fans climb escalators in the mall, put lives at risk, security lapses exposed
stories.summary: A dangerous fan frenzy erupted during Akshay Kumar’s event at Gaur City Mall on Friday, raising serious concerns about crowd management and fan safety. The actor was at the venue to promote his film Bhoot Bangla, accompanied by co-stars Rajpal Yadav and Wamiqa Gabbi. Within minutes of their arrival, the crowd swelled beyond control, creating a chaotic, stampede-like situation. Fans were seen climbing escalators and pushing through packed areas, putting their lives at risk and exposing serious lapses in security arrangements. The situation worsened, leading to a stampede-like situation. People were seen putting their lives at risk. The viral video showed some fans climbing onto the escalator railings for a better view. Barricades on the ground floor broke, and people pushed each other forward. This situation could have turned into a major accident. The biggest question is whether there were proper security arrangements for such public events? Thousands of people gathering in a closed space and the loss of control raises questions about the preparations of the mall management and event organisers. After the video went viral on social media, users appeared angry. Many called it irresponsible and said that stars and their teams should prioritise the safety of fans at such events. However, during this time, Akshay Kumar appeared calm on stage and continued to interact with fans. But the crowd getting out of control is a big warning. The film 'Bhoot Bangla' is scheduled to release on April 17. But the pictures that emerged during the promotion raise questions: Is it right to put people's lives at risk in the name of stardom?

stories.title: Gorakhpur to turn waste into fuel:New plan targets pollution, cleaner city
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has launched a new ‘RDF Roadmap’ to strengthen scientific waste disposal and curb pollution in the city. The plan focuses on converting waste into fuel, helping make Gorakhpur cleaner and more environment-friendly. The roadmap was unveiled at a round-table conference organised by the Municipal Corporation along with Environmental Management Center Private Limited at a hotel in the Gorakhnath area. The initiative aims to improve solid waste management while reducing pollution levels. Waste to be used as alternative fuel Mayor Dr Shrivastava said waste should no longer be seen as something to discard, but as a resource. Under the plan, Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) and torrefied charcoal made from waste will be used as an alternative to coal in cement industries. This is expected to reduce pollution and ease the burden on landfill sites. The scheme is linked to the National Clean Air Programme and the Swachh Bharat Mission. The civic body is working to develop Gorakhpur into a ‘zero waste’ and sustainable city, setting an example for others. Focus on waste segregation at source The Municipal Corporation is putting strong emphasis on segregating waste at the household level. Door-to-door collection of separated waste is being promoted, along with plans to expand the capacity of waste processing plants to convert more waste into fuel. Additional Municipal Commissioner Pramod Kumar said the roadmap will also strengthen transportation, quality testing, and supply systems. This will ensure industries receive a steady supply of high-quality RDF and make the process more organised. Steps to curb open waste burning Officials said the initiative will help reduce open burning and dumping of waste, which are major contributors to air pollution. By promoting scientific waste management and reuse, the plan also supports a circular economy. Experts at the conference shared suggestions to improve waste management and stressed the need for effective implementation of the new system.

stories.title: Badaun Health officer’s wife dies in car fire:Woman screamed amid the flames; husband severely injured
stories.summary: A 25-year-old woman died after a moving car caught fire in Uttar Pradesh’s Badaun district in the early hours of Friday. Her husband, a Community Health Officer, managed to escape but sustained serious burn injuries. The incident took place around 1 am near Rauta village in the Usait police station area. The car was being driven by Arpit Bhardwaj (28), while his wife Priya was lying on the back seat. First see 3 pictures... Wife unable to exit car According to police, Priya had undergone a kidney stone operation three days ago at a private hospital in Palia in Lakhimpur Kheri. The couple was returning home after her discharge when the car caught fire. Arpit managed to get out of the vehicle after it caught fire. Priya, who was on the back seat, could not exit the car. Police said the rear doors appeared to be locked, and she was unable to open them despite repeated attempts. Locals alerted, rescue unsuccessful Locals reached the spot after noticing the flames but could not rescue her. Police and fire brigade teams were informed and reached the site. By the time the fire was brought under control, Priya had died. Arpit, who suffered burn injuries, has been admitted to a hospital. Family travelled in separate vehicles Family members said Priya’s condition after surgery had led them to travel in separate vehicles. Arpit’s parents and their one-and-a-half-year-old daughter had reached home earlier in another car. Cause of fire under investigation Station House Officer Devendra Singh said the exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. “Prima facie, a short circuit or technical fault is suspected. A detailed technical examination of the vehicle will be conducted,” he said.

stories.title: ‘Not a single Miyan, but named Miyanpur’:CM Yogi renames village in Lakhimpur as 'Rabindranagar'; Bangladeshi Hindus receive land rights
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday announced that Miyanpur village in the Mohammadi assembly constituency will be renamed Rabindranagar. Addressing a gathering, Adityanath criticised the Congress, alleging that the village was named Miyanpur to “hide identity”. “There is not a single ‘Miyan’ here, yet it was named Miyanpur. This will now change,” he said. He added that the village would be renamed after Rabindranath Tagore, “who gave India its national anthem”, to reflect a new identity. The Chief Minister was in Lakhimpur to attend two programmes. In Miyanpur, he distributed land ownership certificates to 331 Bangladeshi Hindu families, granting them legal rights over their land. Earlier, in Palia, he handed over land ownership certificates to 4,356 families from the Tharu tribe and 2,350 families of freedom fighters’ dependents. During the visit, Adityanath also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 538 development projects worth Rs 1,311 crore. This included the inauguration of 345 projects valued at Rs 356 crore and the foundation laying for 193 projects worth Rs 955 crore. Read the key points of CM Yogi's speech: CM Yogi distributed ownership certificates to Tharu people for their land rights. Tharu women also gifted handmade items. 1- Hindus and Sikhs suffered due to the deeds of Pakistan CM Yogi said, “Pakistan, through its actions, caused the partition of India. That same Pakistan has itself been divided, and more divisions may follow. But who suffered the consequences? Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, Parsis and Christians living there suffered, because no other community has a presence there.” 2- Miyanpur will now be Rabindranagar Yogi said, “Look at how wrongdoing speaks for itself. These people were rejected by Bangladesh and persecuted due to Pakistan’s actions. They came as displaced persons, and their ancestral properties were seized. Congress committed injustice — they took your votes but never gave you ownership rights. To hide your identity, the village was named Miyanpur. Think about it — not a single ‘Miyan’, yet the name was Miyanpur. Now it will be renamed Rabindranagar. You will be identified with Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, who gave India its national anthem. Bengal is the land of India’s spiritual and cultural heritage. The national anthem was written by Rabindranath Tagore, and the national song by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.” 3- MLAs will start drooling Addressing the Tharu community in Palia, CM Yogi spoke about connecting them with industries and businesses. Praising local MLA Romi Sahni, he also made a light remark: “You will see, as soon as Romi ji’s bakery opens, public representatives sitting on stage will start drooling. He makes excellent sweets. When the issue of giving you land titles was being discussed, he even came to me with a box of sweets. Now those same sweets will be made here.” The CM added that the day is special as it precedes Maharana Sanga’s birth anniversary, making the distribution of land rights even more significant. 4- No one will be able to grab your land now The Chief Minister said that neither the Forest Department, Police, nor Revenue officials will interfere in people’s rights anymore. Illegal land grabbing and manipulation will be stopped. He added, “According to scriptures, the best governance is where people are happy. The success of governance lies in public welfare.” 5- Generations struggled for this land The CM said that several generations have struggled for land rights. Families of freedom fighters and the Tharu community were deprived for decades, but now this long struggle is being fulfilled. 6- Identity of Chandan Chowki, tribute to Maharana Sanga The CM said Chandan Chowki represents Palia’s identity, where tribal culture, self-respect and the fertility of the Terai region come together. Earlier, the Tharu community faced harassment from officials and struggled for identity. He again noted that receiving land rights on the eve of Maharana Sanga’s birth anniversary is a matter of pride. 7- Settled earlier, but rights were denied Yogi said that people who sacrificed everything during the freedom struggle were later denied their rights. During British rule, their lands were seized, they were tortured, sent to Cellular Jail (Kala Pani), executed, or exiled without trial. After Independence, they were resettled but not given ownership rights. The Tharu community was promised land in 1976 but did not receive ownership. Similarly, freedom fighters settled in eastern Uttar Pradesh in 1955 were also denied rights. “Those who sacrificed for the nation were deprived even in independent India,” he said. 8- Previous governments focused only on family interests Yogi said previous governments lacked sensitivity and prioritised family interests over public welfare. “They divided society, took away your rights and resources, and created an identity crisis. But today, the double-engine government is giving shape to your dreams by granting land rights.” He added that: 9- Development was earlier limited to one village CM Yogi said earlier development was concentrated in one place. “Today, 25 crore people are our family. Earlier, development and planning were centred only in Saifai, where one family benefited at the cost of the poor.” 10- Tharu community to be linked with bakery industry The CM said this initiative is not just about rights but also about development. He praised Romi Sahni for setting an example and said, “I want you to establish a model around Chandan Chowki that brings self-reliance to the Tharu community. By connecting with your bakery, we can expand business across the Terai region and Uttarakhand.” 11- Announcement to withdraw cases CM Yogi said that cases filed against members of the Tharu community during the Samajwadi Party government will be withdrawn. He alleged that the previous government protected criminals and filed false cases against innocent people. “I assure you, no one will be able to oppress you now,” he said.

stories.title: 'I received threats for raising cow protection issue':Shankaracharya says governments now want to act as religious leaders
stories.summary: In Rajasthan, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has said that he is receiving death threats if he visits Uttar Pradesh (UP). He said that he is being warned that he would be killed for speaking in favour of cow protection. He also commented on Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, saying that he is becoming a “meat seller wearing saffron clothes”. ‘Hinduism is being followed according to govt circulars’ He further said that today Hinduism is being followed according to government circulars instead of scriptures. He added that governments now want to act as religious authorities themselves. According to him, in Hindu tradition, the king and the religious teacher were always separate, and this system is now being changed, which he said cannot be accepted. The Shankaracharya is currently in Kota, where he spoke openly about Sanatan Dharma, Hinduism, the role of government, conflicts with saints, and the threats he claims to be receiving. Read- Conversation with Shankaracharya Q: What is the current situation of Sanatan Dharma? Is religion getting stronger in the country or facing challenges? A: The teachings of Sanatan Dharma come from the Vedas, and from Veda-based Puranas, Smritis and other literature. Today’s so-called Hindutva is not following scriptures properly. Instead, it is being followed according to government circulars. If Hindus follow circulars, they will have no protection. Only those who follow scriptures are true Hindus. Q: You have mentioned a “Dharma Yudh Board”. Is this becoming a major movement? A: It has already started. Now it depends on how deeply the people involved work for it. Results will follow accordingly. Q: Are attempts being made to suppress your voice? Have you also received threats recently? A: Attacks are being made one after another. Sometimes cases are filed, sometimes allegations are made, and sometimes death threats are given. We cannot remain silent out of fear. We are only saying what is written in the scriptures. If scriptures call the cow a mother, why is it being treated as an animal? How is cow slaughter and trade being justified in the name of tradition? Q: Are religious places being run by governments? A: Yes, governments are trying to control religious institutions. They want to become religious authorities themselves. In Hindu tradition, the king and the religious teacher were separate, but now this is being changed. Religious authority should remain with saints, while governance should remain with leaders. Q: How do you see the Prayagraj bathing incident? Was it an administrative failure or political pressure? A: If it was only an administrative mistake, the administration would have justified and investigated it, but that did not happen. No inquiry or action was taken. The Chief Minister publicly stated in the Assembly that everything happened according to his direction. Q: Even after this controversy, there have been multiple cases and disputes? A: Multiple cases have been filed, allegations have been made, and now there are death threats saying I will be killed if I visit Uttar Pradesh. All this is happening for speaking about Sanatan Dharma. Q: Yogi Adityanath is also a saint, isn’t he? A: A true saint cannot support animal slaughter or meat trade. Even a temple priest does not do such work. A true Hindu hesitates even before killing a mosquito. If someone is involved in large-scale animal slaughter and trade, calling them a saint is not appropriate. The definition of Hinduism is being changed, and this cannot be accepted.
